name: contrarian-trend-subsignals
rationale: Every mechanism this pipeline has tried on the trend family has changed its GAIN; none has ever changed its SIGN. trend-weighted-subsignals (rejected 2026-09-08, that run's worst result on every axis), trend-weight-half (rejected 2026-09-09) and mean-reversion-weighted-subsignals (the current 1.0 / 0.25 split, PR #12) all answer 'how much should the trend family count?' and all of them implicitly assume the answer is a non-negative number. The accumulated evidence says that assumption is the thing worth testing. Today's baseline at the 500,000 JPY diagnostic capital makes 789 trades at a win rate of 0.107 -- systematically wrong-sided, not noisy -- for sharpe_minus_static_mix of -26.27; the 5,000,000 JPY run reads 0.110 and -19.94; and 2026-09-13's ta-weight-085-signal-amplitude established that AMPLIFYING this composite makes the result dramatically worse (Sharpe -14.034 absolute, drawdown +7.82pp), which is what a signal with negative edge does when you turn up its gain. A composite that reliably loses to its own exposure held statically is either uninformative (in which case flipping a sign changes nothing but noise) or informative with the wrong sign (in which case flipping is the single highest-value change available). arXiv:2608.21888 supplies the mechanism that would make the second case true rather than a curve-fit: it measures short-horizon crypto dynamics as reversal-dominant at exactly the sampling frequencies shirube trades, reports that 'the signal lives in signs, not magnitudes', and finds 90% of 183 Binance USDT pairs carry significant directional reversal at a 15-minute horizon against 2.7% of 187 US stocks/ETFs. shirube's SMA cross, EMA cross and MACD histogram sub-signals are momentum readings -- price above its reference line reads BULLISH -- which is the opposite sign to what that measurement implies for this asset class and horizon, and shirube's own pre-holdout lag-1 autocorrelation of 1-minute returns (-0.0147, measured for reversion-horizon-15m over 2026-08-09 .. 2026-08-27, strictly before any holdout window) agrees in sign. This hypothesis inverts ONLY the three trend-family sub-signals (v -> 1.0 - v) and leaves the two mean-reverting ones, both family weights, every indicator period and every zone parameter untouched, so the measured difference is attributable to the trend family's sign alone. Note that it is deliberately NOT the same change as inverting the composite: with the families already opposed, flipping the trend family makes all five sub-signals agree in direction, which should WIDEN the realised composite band rather than mirror it. Expected direction on turnover is therefore upward, keeping it clear of the promotion rule's 50%-of-baseline trade-count floor that rejected both of 2026-09-14's improving variants. Honest caveat to carry into the report: the paper's own economic conclusion is that this edge is roughly 1.3bp per trade against a 5bp round-trip cost and is NOT exploitable net of spot costs, so a sign flip is not expected to make the strategy profitable -- at best it makes it less wrong, and shirube's own backtest gate decides, not the paper's numbers.
code_change_summary: In TradingEngine::compute_btc_target (src/trading/engine.rs), invert the three trend-family sub-signal VALUES at the point where they are pushed onto `sub_signals`, and change nothing else. Concretely: the SMA-cross push becomes `1.0 - damped_cross((close - sma) / sma)`, the EMA-cross push becomes `1.0 - damped_cross((close - ema) / ema)`, and the MACD-histogram push becomes `1.0 - damped_cross(hist / bb_middle)` in the scaled arm AND `1.0 - step` in the no-bb_middle fallback arm (equivalently, flip that arm's step mapping so hist > 0.0 yields 0.0 and hist < 0.0 yields 1.0, with 0.5 unchanged at exactly zero). Prefer expressing this as a single named private helper, e.g. `fn contrarian(v: f64) -> f64 { 1.0 - v }`, applied at all four sites, so the diff reads as one decision rather than four. Do NOT touch the RSI sub-signal, the Bollinger %B sub-signal, damped_cross itself, CROSS_SATURATION, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, which family weight each sub-signal is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation, the empty-sub_signals warmup guard returning None, the sentiment combination, or the final clamp. Note that 1.0 - v maps [0.0, 1.0] onto itself, so every sub-signal remains in range by construction and the aggregation's range guarantee is unaffected -- say so in a comment. Document the change with a NOTE comment naming this hypothesis, stating the mechanism (crypto short-horizon dynamics measured as reversal-dominant; the trend family's momentum sign is the hypothesis under test) and citing arXiv:2608.21888 along with the caveat that the paper reports this edge as sub-cost. Update the function's doc comment accordingly. Add unit tests in the same module: (a) a point with close well above both sma and ema and a positive histogram, asserting the trend contribution is now BEARISH (each inverted sub-signal < 0.5) and that the returned composite is below what the pre-change formula gave for the same point; (b) the mirror case with close well below both reference lines; (c) a point where the relative gap is exactly zero, asserting the inverted value is still exactly 0.5 (1.0 - 0.5), i.e. the inversion is neutral-preserving; (d) a point supplying ONLY RSI and Bollinger %B, asserting the result is byte-identical to the pre-change formula because no trend sub-signal is present; (e) the MACD fallback arm with bb_middle = None and a positive histogram, asserting it now contributes 0.0 rather than 1.0. Update any existing compute_btc_target_* test whose expected value legitimately changes -- do not weaken or delete a test to make it pass. Instrument and REPORT (via stderr logging or a scratch harness -- do not add a field to BacktestReport for this) the realised min/max/sd of ta_normalized over the evaluated window, so the report can state whether the composite band widened from the 2026-09-14 measurement of [0.3359, 0.6548] as the rationale predicts.
constraints: This hypothesis DOES modify TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's body. That is permitted under experiments/hypotheses/README.md's '`compute_btc_target` may be modified' section, but ONLY on this hypothesis's own dedicated isolation: "worktree" branch, and it MUST be reported explicitly so the coordinator flags it in any PR description.
MUST NOT change compute_btc_target's SIGNATURE. Only its body may change.

MUST NOT change the RSI or Bollinger %B sub-signal formulas, damped_cross, CROSS_SATURATION, REVERSION_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, TREND_SUBSIGNAL_WEIGHT, the family weight each sub-signal is pushed with, the weighted-mean aggregation, the sentiment combine and its clamp, apply_zone, sticky_target, allocation_delta_to_order, the lot-size check, the orders_below_min counting arm, the RiskManager call sequence, or the fee logic. Only the SIGN of the three trend-family sub-signal values may change.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including every existing compute_btc_target_* unit test. Update an expected value only where the inversion legitimately changes it, and do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass.

MUST NOT fit anything on the holdout window, or on any window at all. This change introduces no tunable constant -- the inversion is exact (1.0 - v) and is not a parameter to be scaled. If a partial inversion seems better, that is a separate hypothesis to propose, not a value to tune mid-run.
MUST NOT change src/signal/engine.rs's broadcast cadence or anything about live scheduling.

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically -- a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff touches compute_btc_target's body, that it REVERSES the direction of three sub-signals, and that it therefore changes the allocation target the live engine acts on in a way a reviewer must scrutinise before it reaches real money.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the order-submission mechanics themselves.

paper_reference.title: Short-horizon mean reversion in cryptocurrency markets: a matched cross-market measurement
paper_reference.key_claim: Short-horizon directional dynamics in crypto are reversal-dominant and far stronger than in equities -- 90% of 183 Binance USDT pairs carry significant directional reversal at a 15-minute horizon against 2.7% of 187 US stocks/ETFs -- and 'the signal lives in signs, not magnitudes': lag-one return autocorrelation is near zero on the major coins (-0.046 crypto vs -0.009 equities) yet simply betting against the previous candle captures most of the effect.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset class and the same sampling frequencies shirube actually trades, with a recent sample (2025-01-01 .. 2026-02-11 primary, 2026-02-12 .. 2026-08-08 frozen holdout), four-venue cross-validation, exact permutation nulls and multi-year stability tests -- unusually well-evidenced for this literature. Crucially it speaks to SIGN rather than to magnitude or weighting, which is the one dimension of the trend family this pipeline has never tested: three prior hypotheses all varied its gain and none could have detected a sign error. It needs no new indicator, config field, or learned model -- the change is 1.0 - v at three existing sites. Its direction is independently corroborated inside shirube by the -0.0147 lag-1 autocorrelation of 1-minute bitFlyer bars measured over pre-holdout data for reversion-horizon-15m.
paper_reference.cons: The paper's own economic conclusion argues against expecting profit from this: the gross edge peaks near 1.3bp per trade against a 5bp round-trip cost, 'not exploitable under benchmark spot-cost assumptions', and it vanishes entirely at the 10-20bp taker band -- which is where shirube actually trades, so the paper predicts a sign flip makes the strategy less wrong rather than profitable. The instrument differs (183 Binance USDT pairs vs bitFlyer BTC/JPY spot), the mechanism tested is a constrained autoregressive logit over the previous 12 candles' returns rather than an SMA/EMA/MACD composite passed through a zone allocator, and the authors offer NO trading remedy at all -- they read the residual as compensation for supplying immediacy, competed down to the cost of competing for it. Mapping 'reversal-dominant at short horizons' onto 'invert the trend sub-signals' is this pipeline's translation, not the authors'. No number from the paper is used as evidence; shirube's own backtest gate decides.
